From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Product Eng <product-eng@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transitional pricing accommodation for Novo Networks — data residency hold

Team — looping you in on a sticky ask from Novo Networks (deal ND-4791). Short summary below; details and attachments after.

Summary:
- Novo planned a private VPC deployment in our EU region for a regulated pilot next quarter. They passed security and procurement, but the EU data-residency enforcement (customer-managed routing + region pinning) we promised in the SOW is slipping by at least 8–12 weeks due to an unexpected dependency in the control-plane rollout.
- Customer cannot proceed with the production pilot without the residency guarantee. They are asking for a commercial accommodation to bridge the gap so they can retain go-live slot and not pause contracts with their customers.

What Novo is asking (customer ask):
- Either a timebound discount on hosted inference rates until residency is available, or a one-time credit to cover the period they must remain on hosted endpoints while they wait for the VPC feature.
- They prefer a simple 30% discount for up to 3 months but are open to other structures.

My ask to this thread:
1) Product: confirm the expected ETA window (best-case / conservative) for EU residency enforcement and whether a rollback/fallback plan is possible earlier than the current estimate. I put product-eng on To.
2) Finance/Monica: can you run a cost/ margin impact for a 30% discount for 3 months vs a fixed one-time credit (we can propose either). Also advise on approval process and who must sign (is this an exec-level concession?).
3) Marissa/Aditya: need guidance on whether we can provisionally offer a bridging rate (simple customer-facing language) while we finalize internal approvals. Customer is pushing to get formal wording by EOD Wednesday their time (Thu 24 Jun PT).

Attachments: SOW_v1.pdf (customer SOW with residency clause), impact_summary.csv (usage profile and monthly spend estimate).

Customer contacts: Claire Zhang (buyer), James Li (technical lead). I also pasted their ask below.

--
Karthik

Subject: Re: Transitional pricing accommodation for Novo Networks — data residency hold

Thanks Karthik — quick take from finance.

I ran two quick scenarios against the usage numbers in impact_summary.csv:
- Option A: 30% off hosted inference rates for 3 months — estimated gross margin hit ~46% of expected revenue for the period (net impact ~-$68k).
- Option B: One-time credit sized to expected overage for the wait period (estimate we used: prorated monthly spend x 2 months) — net impact ~-$42k.

Notes/questions:
- Which of these is easier for Sales to communicate? Credits are easier to track in billing but discounting is simpler for the customer to understand.
- If this is approved, we need a documented approval chain: does this require VP Sales + CFO? Or, per current concession policy, can Marissa approve up to $50k one-off?
- I also need product confirmation on conservative timeline. If this ends up > 3 months the numbers change materially.

If helpful I can produce an approval memo template and attach a short customer-facing note we can send provisionally ("subject to final exec sign-off").

—Monica
Director, Finance Operations
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Transitional pricing accommodation for Novo Networks — data residency hold

Karthik / Monica / Product — thanks for the fast analysis. My position: we should keep Novo in the funnel and avoid a procurement restart. I support a provisional bridge, with a firm cap and timebox. Proposed approach:

1) Offer a provisional one-time credit sized as Option B (~$42k) OR a 30% discount for up to 8 weeks (not the full 3 months) — whichever the customer prefers.
2) Credit language: "Redwood will provide a one-time commercial accommodation to Novo Networks to offset hosting costs incurred while we complete EU data-residency enforcement. This accommodation is time-limited and contingent on the roadmap ETA of the feature; acceptance requires a signed addendum to the SOW."
3) Approval: Marissa to approve up to $50k one-off; anything above requires Aditya + Finance sign-off. Monica, if you confirm Option B is <= $50k we can proceed with provisional customer communication.

Karthik — please prepare the short customer note (I can review) and include the specific dollar amount you want to propose. If Novo accepts, we'll route the approval memo to Aditya for final sign-off.

-Marissa
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Marissa / Team — reviewed. I approve a one-time credit up to $50k for Novo Networks to bridge for EU residency latency, subject to:
- Karthik to confirm the proposed credit amount and attach the customer-facing addendum language;
- Monica to confirm the entry code in billing and that the accounting treatment is documented;
- Karthik to secure a signed addendum to the SOW (legal can help with a short form).

Karthik, please send a draft note to Claire (copied to procurement) that says we will provide a one-time commercial accommodation of $45,000 (example amount within approved cap) while we finalize the EU residency feature. Use the language Marissa proposed and mark the offer as contingent on the signed addendum. Once Claire confirms, circle back so we can route the approval memo and post the billing credit.
